scope: Byte-exact original-backed A1 Weyl-owner regressions for the cold canonical-dual sharing positive case and the independently prewarmed dual-owner rejection case. The two cases are inseparable: accepting every structurally equal datum would violate the negative case. These goldens release no mathematical, cache, rank or performance gate until a tests-first BEFORE and semantic AFTER run on HPC.

regression_assertions: Both warm-source/cold-target canonical-dual histories share one compatible Weyl owner.
Equality returns true and inequality returns false in both dual-construction directions (SC to adjoint and adjoint to SC).
Both products succeed and have identity word [].
The saved Weyl element retains its original root-datum owner after the source variable is rebound.
The complete stdout matches byte-for-byte and stderr is exactly zero bytes.
cases.before_requirement: The unchanged Rust implementation must fail the complete original-backed comparison while reaching WC_RECOVERY|727 exactly once.

ordered_oracle_diagnostics: Runtime:Negative integer where unsigned is required
regression_assertions: An independently prewarmed structurally equal owner remains incompatible.
Binary equality, inequality and multiplication each reject with Weyl group mismatch before producing an operation value.
Invalid high and negative words preserve their distinct ordered diagnostics.
Every rejection recovers and the complete stdout and stderr match byte-for-byte.
cases.before_requirement: The unchanged Rust implementation must fail the complete original-backed comparison while reaching WCN_RECOVERY|733 exactly once.

required_gate_sequence: HPC tests-first BEFORE: the frozen original must reproduce all four golden streams and unchanged Rust must fail exactly the two named regressions while the retained control passes.
Smallest owning semantic repair: do not combine cache or performance changes.
HPC semantic AFTER: the same two regressions and retained control must pass against the unchanged original goldens.
Only after semantic AFTER may same-rank profiling or broader G2/B2/C2 coverage proceed.
